info.name: OpenSOP API
info.description:
Complete OpenSOP REST API collection. Import into Yaak (File → Import → pick this file), Postman, Insomnia, or Bruno.

## Setup

1. Select the environment (`OpenSOP Local` or `OpenSOP Production`).
2. If you're running in strict auth mode, set `sop_token` in the environment.
3. Use the requests in order — Discovery → Start Instance → Submit Steps → Inspect State.

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | Origin of the OpenSOP server |
| `sop_token` | Value for the `X-SOP-Token` header. Leave blank in dev mode. |
| `process_name` | The process to operate on (default: `customer-onboarding`) |
| `instance_id` | Set automatically by the "Start Instance" test script, or paste manually |
| `step_id` | The step id to submit (default: `collect-business-info`) |
| `callback_id` | UUID from a `Sop::Callback` — set after a webhook step creates one |

Full docs: see `docs/API.md` and `docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md` in the OpenSOP repository.

item.name: Discovery
item.description: Read-only endpoints for discovering what processes exist and their schemas. Start here.

request.description: Returns every active process (latest version per name) with a summary of inputs, outputs, tags, and SLA. Use this to discover available processes before fetching schemas.

Returns the full YAML-derived definition for a single process as JSON. Agents use this to understand inputs, outputs, and step shapes before calling /start.

Optional query param: `version=1.0` to pin a specific version. Without it, latest wins.

item.name: Execution
item.description: Core runtime endpoints. Start an instance, inspect its state, submit outputs for human-gated steps.

request.description:
Starts a new instance. Validates inputs against the process schema, creates the instance, and advances through any auto-executing prefix (automated steps before the first human-gated step).

The test script captures the returned `id` into the `instance_id` environment variable so subsequent requests use it automatically.

**Body fields:**
- `inputs` (object, required): key-value pairs matching the process's declared `inputs`
- `metadata` (object, optional): free-form tracking metadata

Returns 201 with the instance state (which may already include a paused step waiting for input).
Second example using the `lead-qualification` process (3 steps instead of 6). Useful for testing end-to-end flow quickly.

Full current state of an instance, including every step. Poll this while waiting on long-running work.

The response has the same shape as `POST /start`: top-level instance fields + `steps` array.

**State progression:**
- Instance: `pending` → `running` → `completed` | `failed` | `cancelled`
- Step: `pending` → `active` → `completed` | `failed` | `skipped`

An `active` step has a `sub_state` (`waiting_for_input`, `waiting_for_callback`, `escalated`, etc.) explaining why it's still active.
Compact view — just the steps array, no instance envelope. Use when you only need step state.

Submit outputs for the `collect-business-info` form step. The engine validates outputs against the declared step schema, marks the step completed, and advances to the next step.

**Body fields:**
- `outputs` (object, required): keys matching the step's declared outputs
- `decided_by` (string, optional): who made the decision — free-form, e.g. `human:ops-lead` or `agent:onboarding-copilot`
- `confidence` (number 0-1, optional): for judgment steps; below `confidence_threshold` may trigger escalation

The response shows both the updated step AND the instance state after all cascading auto-advances.

Submit a judgment step decision. `decision` must be one of the declared enum values (`approve`, `reject`, `request-more-info` for customer-onboarding). If the step's `condition:` downstream is `decision == 'approve'`, the webhook step will be entered next.

Submit the lead-qualification form step. This is a 3-step process — submitting this one typically advances straight to completion (score-lead runs automatically, notify-team runs automatically).

Check the response — `instance.state` should be `completed` and `instance.outputs` should contain `score` and `qualified`.

Cancel an instance. Sets `state` to `cancelled`, records the reason, marks any active steps as `skipped`. Does NOT roll back side effects that already happened.

Returns 422 if the instance is already in a terminal state (completed/failed/cancelled).
List instances across all processes, sorted by most recent first. Supports filtering.

item.name: List running instances for a process

request.description:
Filter by `state` and/or `process`. Useful for building ops dashboards:
- `state=running` → what's in-flight
- `state=failed` → what needs attention
- `state=completed&process=customer-onboarding` → audit trail
Dashboard-style query to surface what's gone wrong. Each instance's `error` field has the failure message; drill into the instance to see which step failed and why.

item.name: Webhooks
item.description:
Inbound webhook callback receiver. Third parties (compliance providers, KYC vendors) POST results here.

**Note:** these endpoints do NOT require `X-SOP-Token` — third parties wouldn't know it. Auth is bypassed specifically for this path.

item.name: Receive webhook callback (simulating a compliance provider)

request.description:
Simulates a third-party compliance provider posting results back to OpenSOP.

**Setup:** Before this works, you need a webhook step that's in `waiting_for_callback` state. Start a customer-onboarding instance, submit the form, submit the judgment as `approve`, then check `GET /sop/:name/:id/steps` — the `submit-to-compliance` step should be in `sub_state=waiting_for_callback`. Find its callback URL in the `Sop::Callback` row (query the DB or visit `/instances/:id` in the UI to see it), then paste the UUID part after `/sop/webhooks/` into the `callback_id` environment variable.

**Body:** keys should match the webhook step's declared `outputs:` — in this case, `entity_id` and `compliance_status`.

**Responses:**
- 200: `{ "status": "received" }` — callback processed, instance advanced
- 404: no pending callback at that path (wrong id, or already received)
- 409: callback already resolved (received or expired)
- 422: payload didn't match declared outputs (raw payload persisted on the callback row for recovery)

Same as above but returns a rejection. When `compliance_status: rejected` flows back, the subsequent `create-account` step's condition (`compliance_status == 'approved'`) evaluates false, so the step is skipped. The instance ends in `completed` state with `outputs.status = "rejected"`.
